Sinite
SY-nyte
n. (proper name; one of the eleven Canaanite peoples descended from Canaan)
Hebrew Sini, a gentilic from an unidentified place-name Sin. Not connected with Sinai, nor with the Wilderness of Sin.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The Sinite is named once in each of the two parallel lists: “And the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite” (Genesis 10:17), with 1 Chronicles 1:15. Canaan's descendants are eleven peoples — Sidon and Heth first, then the Jebusite, Amorite, Girgasite, Hivite, Arkite, Sinite, Arvadite, Zemarite, and Hamathite. These are the nations Israel was commanded to dispossess, and the Sinite is one of the five whose territory is never again mentioned. The Authorized Version prints the name and passes on. The dictionary notes what the list establishes. The conquest of Canaan was not an arbitrary land-grab; Genesis 15:16 says Abraham's seed would wait four hundred years because “the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full,” and Leviticus 18 catalogues what filled it. God named these peoples in Noah's generation, bore with them for centuries, and judged them at last through Joshua. A nation that vanishes from the record without a single narrative of its own is still a nation God numbered, warned, and dealt with justly.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Sinite is a proper name and has no entry in Webster's dictionary of the English language.

expand to see more

Sinite is a Hebrew gentilic proper name; Webster's 1828 dictionary treats common English words and does not define it.

The name appears at Genesis 10:17 and 1 Chronicles 1:15.

The Sinites are one of the eleven peoples descended from Canaan, son of Ham.

Their neighbours in the list are the Hivite and the Arkite.

The name has no connection with Sinai or the Wilderness of Sin.

Key Scripture

Gen 10:17 — "And the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,"

1Ch 1:15 — "And the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,"

Gen 15:16 — "But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full."

Modern Corruption

The conquest of Canaan is widely charged as ethnic cleansing; Scripture presents it as delayed judgment on named and warned peoples.

expand to see more

The standard modern charge against Joshua is genocide, and it is made without reference to what Scripture actually says about the Canaanites. Genesis 15:16 has God waiting four generations because their iniquity was not yet full; Leviticus 18 lists what filled it; Rahab shows that any Canaanite who feared the LORD was received, and she is in the genealogy of Christ. Judgment deferred for centuries and executed on moral grounds is not what the word cleansing means.

The principle to recover is the patience of God toward nations He eventually judges. He named the Sinites in Noah's generation and gave them four hundred years. The same patience is now extended to the nations of the earth, and the same judgment is appointed.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Sini, a gentilic from an unidentified Sin; one of the eleven Canaanite peoples of Genesis 10:17.

expand to see more

Hebrew Sini, the gentilic ending -i marking a people.

Genesis 10:17 and 1 Chronicles 1:15 are the only occurrences.

Eleven peoples descend from Canaan in the Table of Nations.

Five of them, the Sinite among them, never appear in a narrative.

Genesis 15:16 gives the ground and the timing of their judgment.
